description:
FILED s473s (2026-09-08) from the batch's FULL GATE, which read
`Pl/t/fileio-02.t (Tests: 40 Failed: 1)` — row 15 "in-memory scalar:
seek/tell, zero-fill, overwrite, +< read+write".  PRE-EXISTING on main and
NOT this batch's: reproduced on a `git archive main` (4dee376f) extraction.

REPRODUCER (two lines, and the cold cache is the whole condition):

    $ cat /tmp/fcntl-probe.pl
    use Fcntl qw(SEEK_SET SEEK_END);
    print "ok\n";

    $ rm -rf /tmp/coldcache-probe
    $ PCL_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/coldcache-probe ./runpcl /tmp/fcntl-probe.pl
    Deep recursion on subroutine "Pl::Parser2::_lower_block_1" at Pl/Parser2.pm line 8461.
    ok

perl warns at recursion depth 100.  s473c (#1240, the statement location
register) split `_lower_block` into `_lower_block` + `_lower_block_1`, which
adds ONE frame per nesting level, and core `Fcntl.pm` is nested deeply enough
that the split crosses 100.  The warning is harmless to the OUTPUT — "ok" is
still printed and the transpile is correct — but it is written to STDERR by the
runtime's own `pl2cl --module` child, so it lands in the observed output of any
gate row that runs a program with `2>&1`.

WHY NEITHER s473c's GATE NOR A RE-RUN SEES IT: the module cache.  A warm cache
never re-transpiles `Fcntl.pm`, so the warning never fires; running the file
alone after any earlier run passes.  It appears when the cache is COLD for the
current generation — which is exactly what a generation bump produces, so the
next emission-changing batch after s473c was always going to be the one that
saw it.  s473s is that batch (v2-1030 -> v2-1060); its own change has nothing
to do with block lowering.

VERIFIED BOTH WAYS
  * `PCL_CACHE_DIR=<fresh> prove Pl/t/fileio-02.t` on the main extraction:
    FAILS row 15, same warning.
  * the same file on a warm cache, both trees: PASSES.

FIX SHAPES (not chosen here — s473c's owner should pick):
  (a) make the recursion shallower again — `_lower_block_1` is a tail of
      `_lower_block`, so a lowering that does not add a frame per level would
      restore the old depth;
  (b) `no warnings 'recursion'` at the narrowest scope around the block walker
      (the s403 ruling's second form: tree walkers get `'recursion'`, and the
      precedent is explicit that a blanket handler is not an option);
  (c) leave it and let the gate row tolerate it — REJECTED here: the sin is
      the noise on a child's stderr, which is a row's observed output.
(b) is the smallest and matches the standing rule; (a) is the honest one if the
extra frame is not needed.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: check the other deep-nesting core modules on a cold
cache too (`PCL_CACHE_DIR=<fresh>` plus a `use` of each), not only Fcntl —
the depth is a property of the module, and Fcntl is merely the first one a gate
row happened to capture.


=== DONE (s478, Fable, 2026-09-08) â fix shape (b), at FOUR sites ===
`no warnings 'recursion'` at the head of every per-statement walker, never a
blanket handler (the s403 ruling).  The s473c split was only the FIRST site:
the guard's mechanism rows (150 `my` statements in one block, program mode,
top level and in a sub body) found three MORE that fire on the same input â
`Pl::ClassicSort::_walk`, `Pl::Manifest::_walk`, `Pl::CLForm::_flat` +
`to_string` â all walkers over the emitted form, whose nesting is one level
per `my`.  Sites: Pl/Parser2.pm `_lower_block` (the call into `_lower_block_1`,
which already carried it), Pl/ClassicSort.pm `_walk`, Pl/Manifest.pm `_walk`,
Pl/CLForm.pm `_flat` + `to_string`.
Probed silent at 150 and 1000 statements per block, both shapes; lib/Fcntl.pm
and lib/Errno.pm transpile as modules with an empty compiler stderr.
Guard: Pl/t/module-transpile-quiet-01.t (6 rows; inverse: rows 2, 4, 5, 6
fail on aa58b3b7).  Emission-neutral by construction (a lexical warnings
pragma), corpus-diff IDENTICAL vs aa58b3b7.  The task's NOTE (other deep
core modules on a cold cache) is covered by the mechanism rows: the depth is
a property of the BLOCK LENGTH, and every walker that recurses per statement
now carries the pragma.
subject: s473c's `_lower_block` split pushed `Pl::Parser2::_lower_block_1` past perl's DEEP-RECURSION warning depth on core Fcntl.pm: a COLD module cache prints `Deep recursion on subroutine "Pl::Parser2::_lower_block_1"` on stderr during the runtime's own module transpile, and any gate row that captures the child's stderr FAILS on it (Pl/t/fileio-02.t row 15)
